title: Role-play lab: six debt client conversations
objectives: Answer six debt client conversations using duration, credit quality and tax.
Use the module's scenario answers (Q21–Q25) as trainer-marked practice.
body_md:
In pairs. One person plays the client, the other explains — in plain words, with a rupee example.

| Client says | Explain |
| --- | --- |
| “My debt fund fell 2% this month. I thought debt was safe.” | Find out whether it is a rate move or a credit event, and explain duration. |
| “This credit risk fund shows a 9% yield and my FD gives 7%. Why not put everything there?” | Explain the yield–risk trade-off and sizing: a small slice at most, never essential money. |
| A retiree wants monthly income from ₹60 lakh. | Compare an SWP from a conservative debt fund, a bond ladder and government schemes, without quoting rates you haven't checked. |
| “I need this money for my daughter's college fees in 2 years.” | Choose the category and explain why long duration doesn't fit: short duration, banking & PSU, or a target maturity fund matched to the date. |
| “What happened in the Franklin Templeton case? Could it happen to me?” | Explain liquidity risk and today's safeguards honestly: side-pocketing, the PRC matrix, stricter liquidity requirements. |
| “A website is selling a bank bond at 10%. It's a bank, so it's safe, right?” | Check whether it's an AT1 bond and explain write-off risk: a bank bond is not automatically safe. |

> **Investor takeaway:** Quiz scenarios Q21–Q25 (trainer-marked): a scenario answer earns its mark if it covers at least three model points and makes no promise of returns.
example: Role-play the 9% yield question: the extra 2% over an FD is payment for default and liquidity risk — ask what the fund holds to earn it.
say: Match duration to the goal date, credit quality to how essential the money is.
Check current rates rather than quoting from memory.
never: Sell a credit risk fund on yield alone.
Predict interest-rate moves as a reason to buy.

check.q: A client says, “My debt fund fell 2% this month. I thought debt was safe.” How do you respond?
o: Promise a recovery by next month
Check whether it is a rate move or a credit event; explain duration and the seesaw; review duration vs goal; no promise of recovery
check.why: Checks whether it is a rate move or a credit event; explains duration and the seesaw; reviews duration vs goal; no promise of recovery.

check.q: A client wants to move all their FD money into a credit risk fund showing a 9% yield. What do you explain?
o: The yield–risk trade-off; default and liquidity risk; sizing as a small slice at most; not for essential money
That credit risk funds never default
check.why: Yield–risk trade-off; default and liquidity risk; sizing as a small slice at most; not for essential money.

check.q: A retiree wants monthly income from ₹60 lakh. What do you outline?
o: SWP from a conservative debt fund, a bond ladder, and eligible government schemes; check current rates rather than quoting from memory; tax via CA
A credit risk fund for the full amount
An equity fund for regular income
check.why: SWP from a conservative debt fund, bond ladder, eligible government schemes; checks current rates rather than quoting from memory; tax via CA.
